summary: Scoped leave-review audit: a reproduced client workflow bypass and an API context race are closed by server-only atomic review, strict client rules and context-bound requests. This is prototype-rule validation, not a whole-application security certificate.
scope: Leave applications, review decisions and associated attendance-lock checks only.

findings.check: Business logic vs rules / update bypass
findings.issue: An assigned Instructor SDK could directly change pending leave to approved while its attendance month was submitted, bypassing the application transaction.
findings.recommendation: Implemented authenticated backend-only review with transactional membership, trainee and all-month lock checks; client reviewed creates/status edits/deletes are denied.

findings.issue: The previous backendRequest read the workspace after awaiting a token, allowing an old action to target a newly selected workspace. Reproduced with the original function.
findings.recommendation: Implemented immutable captured context, pre-send identity checks and late-response rejection.

findings.issue: Pending client requests previously used date-format validation without logical calendar or 90-day enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Added real calendar validation and 1-90 day checks in rules and shared server policy, preserving bounded schema checks on both creates and updates.

findings.issue: Historical client-authored reviews are not retroactively authenticated or migrated by this change. The wider rule set and institution policies remain outside this scoped audit.
findings.recommendation: Review legacy records and the prototype rules before broad production sharing. Do not import original student data without a separate reviewed migration.

validation.before: Real Emulator assertFails failed because a locked-month direct SDK approval succeeded.
validation.after: See Draft PR #16 for final source CI and staging acceptance results. Attack coverage includes own/foreign/anonymous SDK permissions; direct reviewed creation/update/delete; invalid dates, schema/type/size and span; backend role/tenant denial, actor/time injection, concurrent retry, lock atomicity, missing trainee and in-transaction role revocation.
